title.narrative: Intergrated Nutrition and Health response to address malnutrition in Afar and Amhara regions.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to restore and scale up integrated health and nutrition services for conflict- and drought-affected girls, boys, women, and men in five priority woredas of Afar and Amhara Regions. These areas face critical service disruptions due to insecurity, displacement, and funding gaps—leaving vulnerable populations, including IDPs and host communities, without life-saving care.ltbrgtThe project targets Lasta, Zequala, Kunneba, Dalifage, and Asayita woredas to be implemented by Plan International Ethiopia. It will restore primary health care and nutrition services through facility-based and mobile outreach platforms. Activities include early identification and treatment of acute malnutrition—both Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM)—with strong referral linkages to OTPs and TSFPs. Community-based screening campaigns and regular screening will support the identification of identified cases and referral to therapeutic and supplementary feeding programs.ltbrgtThe project also strengthens stabilization centers with essential SC kits, therapeutic supplies, and trained personnel, while promoting and protecting Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergencies (IYCF-E) through counseling, support groups, community volunteers, and mobilization. Primary health care services will be enhanced with essential medicines and disease surveillance support. Last-mile delivery of life-saving health and nutrition supplies will ensure continuity of care.ltbrgtThis action directly supports the EHF 2025 strategy and Nutrition and Health Cluster priorities by improving access to equitable, life-saving services for at-risk populations in hard-to-reach areas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
